name: Masala soy rice bowl
steps: 1. Soak or boil soy chunks 5-8 min until tender; drain and squeeze. | 2. In an approved cooker or pan, heat a little oil and season tomato/onion with spices. | 3. Add soy chunks and a splash of water; cook 3-4 min. | 4. Serve over hot mess rice.
safety: Make one portion only; no room-temperature leftovers

name: Spicy chicken rice bowl
steps: 1. Cut chicken into small even pieces and season with masala and lemon. | 2. Cook on approved air fryer or induction until center is 74 C. | 3. Add cooked vegetables and a fresh mess rice serving. | 4. Finish with lemon.
safety: Buy and cook chicken same day; no storing leftovers

name: Egg and chana power salad
steps: 1. Obtain freshly cooked eggs and chana. | 2. Dice cucumber and tomato. | 3. Mix chickpeas, chopped eggs, vegetables, lemon and pepper. | 4. Eat immediately.
safety: Use prepared mess chana; do not store mixed salad

name: Cold chickpea cucumber salad
steps: 1. Drain and rinse ready-to-eat chickpeas if packaged. | 2. Chop washed produce. | 3. Mix with ground flaxseed, lemon and spices. | 4. Eat immediately.
safety: Cooked chickpeas must be fresh; no overnight storage

name: Egg oats savoury bowl
steps: 1. Simmer oats in water 4-5 min. | 2. Add vegetables and cook until soft. | 3. Stir in beaten egg and continue cooking until fully set. | 4. Season and eat hot.
safety: Cook egg fully; follow your kettle manual for allowed cooking

name: Instant banana peanut oats
steps: 1. Cover oats with hot water and soften for 3-5 min. | 2. Slice banana. | 3. Mix banana, peanuts and cinnamon. | 4. Eat right away.
safety: Shelf-stable until prepared; no dairy needed

name: High-protein milk oats
steps: 1. Open chilled milk purchased for immediate use. | 2. Soften oats with warm water; allow to cool slightly. | 3. Stir in milk and cinnamon. | 4. Add fruit and consume promptly.
safety: Milk pack says refrigerate below 5 C; do not save leftovers

name: Lemon-pepper chicken
steps: 1. Pat chicken dry with clean paper towel. | 2. Rub lemon, pepper, salt, garlic and oil. | 3. Cook until thickest part reaches 74 C. | 4. Rest 3 min; eat immediately.
safety: Separate raw chicken utensils; no fridge means same-day cooking

name: Tandoori-style chicken
steps: 1. Make a thick paste of curd, spices and lemon. | 2. Coat raw chicken immediately before cooking. | 3. Cook to 74 C internal temperature. | 4. Serve fresh with mess roti or salad.
safety: Do not marinate unrefrigerated for hours

name: Chilli-garlic soy chunks
steps: 1. Soften chunks in boiling water and squeeze. | 2. Cook garlic and vegetables in a little oil. | 3. Stir in soy and spices. | 4. Serve steaming hot.
safety: Use fresh portions; avoid high-sodium sauces in large quantities

name: Soy masala roti wrap
steps: 1. Cook soy masala as in R10. | 2. Spread over two fresh rotis. | 3. Add chopped cucumber and lemon. | 4. Roll tightly and eat.
safety: Do not pack for later without chilling

name: Egg salad chapati roll
steps: 1. Chop freshly boiled eggs. | 2. Mix with diced cucumber and tomato. | 3. Season with lemon and pepper. | 4. Roll in chapatis; eat fresh.
safety: Eggs should not sit at room temperature for extended periods

name: Protein milk banana shake
steps: 1. Buy chilled pouch for same-day use. | 2. Mash banana with a fork. | 3. Shake or blend with the milk and cinnamon. | 4. Drink immediately.
safety: Do not leave milk at room temperature

name: Curd fruit flax bowl
steps: 1. Wash and chop the fruit. | 2. Add fresh cold curd. | 3. Sprinkle ground flaxseed. | 4. Eat immediately.
safety: Buy curd for immediate consumption without fridge

name: Peanut banana pre-football snack
steps: 1. Eat banana 45-90 minutes before football. | 2. Add a modest peanut serving if comfortably digested. | 3. Hydrate with water.
safety: Reduce fat close to kick-off if it causes stomach upset

name: Simple lemon fish bowl
steps: 1. Season fish with lemon and pepper. | 2. Cook fish to 63 C internal temperature or until opaque and flakes. | 3. Serve with fresh hot mess rice and vegetables.
safety: No storage without fridge; fish is optional and expensive

name: Roasted chana salad
steps: 1. Wash and chop vegetables. | 2. Add crunchy roasted chana. | 3. Mix lemon, pepper and flaxseed. | 4. Eat immediately.
safety: All ingredients shelf-stable before cutting except produce

name: Mess dal protein rice plate
steps: 1. Take hot mess dal, rice and cooked vegetables. | 2. Prioritize dal and vegetables first. | 3. Add rice to match your football/training energy needs. | 4. Finish with lemon.
safety: Protein varies significantly with actual mess dal thickness

name: Quick milk-free masala oats
steps: 1. Heat water and add oats. | 2. Cook vegetables in the pot until tender. | 3. Stir in oats and spices; simmer to preferred thickness. | 4. Serve hot.
safety: Use only cookware allowed by hostel rules

name: Chicken chana salad
steps: 1. Cook chicken separately to 74 C. | 2. Combine freshly cooked chana and washed vegetables. | 3. Add sliced hot chicken and lemon. | 4. Eat immediately.
safety: No fridge: cook, eat, discard leftovers

name: Peanut flax energy oats
steps: 1. Soften oats in hot water. | 2. Add sliced banana and peanuts. | 3. Sprinkle ground flaxseed. | 4. Mix and eat.
safety: No refrigeration needed until prepared

name: Three-egg roti breakfast
steps: 1. Take three freshly cooked eggs. | 2. Add two fresh mess chapatis. | 3. Add raw vegetable salad and pepper. | 4. Eat at breakfast.
safety: Three breakfast eggs included in mess as reported

name: Guava curd chaat
steps: 1. Wash and dice guava. | 2. Combine with fresh curd. | 3. Add a little spice and lemon. | 4. Eat immediately.
safety: Requires chilled curd consumed promptly

name: Roasted chana peanut crunch
steps: 1. Portion the chana and peanuts. | 2. Add spice if desired. | 3. Pack dry for between classes.
safety: Shelf-stable snack; watch portions if reducing calories
